what_happened: Job 20261031-001542-anbv, a design job, stopped in planning at round 3. The critic still had one major finding open: which CI run of athena/ci/<job> to use, the push run or a pull_request run. The question was a design decision, not something more planning rounds could settle. The the person running Athena ruled that only the push run counts and never a pull_request run. The the person running Athena then queued the retry 20261031-142712-yf70 with that ruling written in.
cause: Athena has no step that spots an open design question early and sends it to the owner or to a recorded default. The planner and critic keep trading revisions on a question that needs a decision. Nothing records a standing rule for CI run events (push vs pull_request), and the host's different trigger and write behavior for each is not part of what the planner is told. The question was only settled by the the person running Athena after the final round.
prevention: Two changes. (1) Add a recorded default that any check on athena/ci/<job> uses only the push run, never a pull_request run, and give the planner and critic that default. (2) Let the critic mark a finding as "needs decision, not revision". When it does, planning stops at once with the question, the options and a recommended answer, rather than using up the remaining rounds. The the person running Athena's answer is then attached to the retry automatically.
proposed_request: Add a standing default to Athena's defaults: when a job's plan or check reads CI results for athena/ci/<job>, it uses only the push-event run and never a pull_request run. Give this default to the planner and critic briefs, and keep within the prompt token budget. Also make the critic able to label a finding "decision needed". When a finding has that label, planning ends early with the question, the options and a recommended answer written to the job record, instead of running further rounds. Acceptance: (1) a test shows a plan that reads a pull_request run is flagged by the critic against the default; (2) a test shows a "decision needed" finding ends planning before the last round with the question recorded; (3) the brief edits pass the banned-word scan and the token budgets test; (4) existing planning tests still pass.
